title: Kaseya VSA 10 API tokens created
volume: None on a normal day. Admins create tokens for new integrations a few times a year.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: One custom detection rule for Kaseya VSA 10, on the CloudAudit records the library's VSA 10 parsers write from its audit log. It makes a detection when someone creates an API token. It matches sensor type Kaseya VSA 10 only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Kaseya VSA 10 parsers and the example bridge in bridges/kaseya-vsa10-audit-logs, and run the bridge with a VSA 10 API token, as the parser entry says. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.

How it works:
- The parsers write the audit log's category, such as Api Tokens, as the event name and the user as the user, and keep the event description in additional_event_data.
- The rule takes an Api Tokens record whose description starts Created API token, so deleted tokens aren't taken.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 4 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 25 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take.
- The events went in through bridges/kaseya-vsa10-audit-logs, run once on the lab machine against a local mock of the VSA 10 API that served the sample events, and posted to HTTP Ingest as gzipped NDJSON, the way the bridge's README says.

Known gaps:
- The bridge polls, so detections arrive up to one poll interval after the event.
- The event descriptions in the samples are made up apart from the API docs' script example, so run the check-your-data search to see the wording your server writes.
